messages:
priya_m: Heads-up — nightly usage job produced ledger skew for ~12 customers. Looks like Stripe invoice items that arrived after the billing cutoff got applied to the wrong period in NetSuite.

nate: Can you paste one example event and the DLQ/log lines?

priya_m: Example log snippet:```2026-03-22T04:00:12Z ERROR usage-processor: late_event id=evt_3Lk9bG source=stripe customer=acct_9xT3 billable_at=2026-03-21T23:59:55Z processed_at=2026-03-22T03:58:10Z billing_window_end=2026-03-21T23:59:00Z```

priya_m: Note billable_at is before midnight cut, but processed_at is > billing_window_end by ~4h. Nightly job currently assumes events processed before run belong to previous window; late arrivals are being attached to today's ledger.

ari: Ugh. We've seen similar when Stripe webhook retries come in from the retry queue after spike. Is this a webhook ordering problem or the nightly job logic?

nate: Looks like nightly job groups by processing timestamp not event billable timestamp. That explains the misattribution. Quick fix is to prefer event.billable_at when present and fall back to processed_at.

sam: Any customers affected with invoices already sent? Need to know refund/credit exposure.

priya_m: 5 customers ended up with incorrect invoice period; some got credits created automatically by the NetSuite integration. I flagged them in the spreadsheet: https://redwood.internal/fin/late-usage-queue (private).

nate: Plan: (1) hotfix nightly job to use billable_at ordering + idempotency guard (2) backfill/reconcile the 12 affected customers with a targeted script (3) add metric for late_event_count and DLQ age. Assigning self for backfill and priya for validation.

ari: I can review the hotfix PR. Also we should patch the webhook consumer to write events to the store with both timestamps so processing is robust.

priya_m: Agree. Also we need a test for out-of-order delivery simulated by Stripe retry bursts.

billing-bot: nightly-run summary 2026-03-22T04:10:05Z — processed=3,421 failed=8 dlq=8 late_event_count=14

nate: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fin-inc/-/pull/482 "usage: prefer billable_at for window attribution" — includes idempotency check keyed by (stripe_event_id, billing_window). @ari please review. :eyes:

ari: Reviewing now. Small comment on the SQL update — prefer an upsert instead of delete/insert to keep audit fields stable.

deploy-bot: Deployed branch pr-482 to staging at 2026-03-22T07:12:04Z. smoke tests passed.

sam: If staging looks good, do we want to run the backfill as a dry-run first and post the diff? I want to confirm there are no double credits.

nate: Yes — will run dry-run tonight 23:00 UTC. Backfill command: `./tools/backfill_usage --since 2026-03-20 --until 2026-03-22 --dry-run --filter late_event=true`

priya_m: I'll validate results and check the 5 impacted customers for invoice/credit health. If all good, switch to live run 01:00 UTC.

sam: Thanks. Please ping finance@redwood once the live run completes so ops can hold manual reversals.

nate: Will do. Assigning follow-ups: nate=backfill, priya=validation, ari=code review + webhook consumer follow-up, sam=customer comms standby.

priya_m: Quick note — added a short-term alert in Datadog: `billing.late_event_rate > 5 for 5m` to catch spikes. :white_check_mark:

nate: Backfill dry-run completed at 2026-03-22T23:45Z — no duplicates in staging output, diff posted to the PR. I'll run live at 01:00 UTC and post update.

sam: Appreciate it.

nate: Live run finished 2026-03-23T01:22Z — reconciled 12 customers, created 0 duplicate credits, 2 invoices required manual adjustment (marked in spreadsheet). Posting final summary shortly. :thumbsup:
